<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par48 />jussive, ''yăqtŭl''; (''c'') a double ‘energetic’ mood of the impf., ''yăqtŭlănnă'' and ''yăqtŭlăn'', in pause ''yăqtŭlā'', the last form thus corresponding to the Hebrew cohortative.

{{GHGmargin-letter|48|c}}
'''3.''' The characteristic of the cohortative form is an ''ā'' ({{GHGheb|text=־ָה}}) affixed to the 1st pers. sing. or plur., e.g. {{GHGheb|text=אֶקְטְלָה}} from {{GHGheb|text=אֶקְטֹל}}.<ref>Probably this ''ā'' goes back to the syllable ''an'', which in Arabic (see above, Rem. to b) is used for the formation of the ‘energetic’ mood, and in Hebrew (see the footnote to {{GHGpar|58|i}}) often stands before suffixes.</ref> It occurs in almost all conjugations and classes of the strong and weak verb (except of course in the passives), and this final {{GHGheb|text=־ָה}} has the tone wherever the afformatives {{GHGheb|text=וּ}} and {{GHGheb|text=־ִי}} would have it. As before these endings, so also before the {{GHGheb|text=־ָה}} cohortative, the movable vowel of the last syllable of the verbal form becomes ''Š<sup>e</sup>wâ'', e.g. in Qal {{GHGheb|text=אֶשְׁמְרָ֫ה|translate=I will observe}}, in Piʿel {{GHGheb|text=נְנַתְּקָ֫ה|translate=let us break asunder}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=2|verse=3}}; on {{GHGheb|text=אֶשְׁקֳטָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=18|verse=4}} {{GHGterm|Q<sup>e</sup>rê}} (cf. also {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=27|verse=4|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ezr|chapter=8|verse=25}}, &c.), see {{GHGpar|10|h}}; with the {{GHGterm|K<sup>e</sup>thîbh}} of these passages, compare the analogous cases {{GHGheb|text=ישׁפוטו}}, &c., {{GHGpar|47|g}}.—On the other hand, an unchangeable vowel in the final syllable is retained as tone-vowel before the {{GHGheb|text=־ָה}}, as (e.g.) in Hiph. {{GHGheb|text=אַזְכִּ֫ירָה|translate=I will praise}}. In pause (as before ''û'' and ''î''), the vowel which became {{GHGterm|Š<sup>e</sup>wâ}} is restored as tone-vowel; thus for the cohortative {{GHGheb|text=אֶשְׁמְרָ֫ה}} the pausal form is {{GHGheb|text=אֶשְׁמֹ֑רָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=59|verse=10}}; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=18|verse=21}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=41|verse=26}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|48|d}}
The change of {{GHGheb|text=־ָה}} into the obtuse {{GHGheb|text=־ֶה}} seems to occur in {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=28|verse=15}}, unless, with Nestle, we are to assume a conflate reading, {{GHGheb|text=וָֽאֶקְרָא}} and {{GHGheb|text=וָֽאֶקְרֶה}}; and with the 3rd pers. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=20|verse=4}}, in a syllable sharpened by a following ''Dageš forte conjunct.''; cf. similar cases of the change of {{GHGheb|text=־ָה}} into the obtuse {{GHGheb|text=־ֶה}} in ''l'' and in {{GHGpar|73|d|doublesign=1}}, {{GHGpar|80|i|nosign=1}}, {{GHGpar|90|i|nosign=1}}. In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=20|verse=4}}, however, {{GHGheb|text=יְדַשְּׁנֶ֫הָ}}—with suffix—is probably intended. An {{GHGheb|text=־ָה}} cohort. is also found with the 3rd pers. in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=5|verse=19}} (twice); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=23|verse=20}}, and again in verse 16 according to the {{GHGterm|Q<sup>e</sup>rê}}, but in both these cases without any effect on the meaning. Probably another instance occurs in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=11|verse=17}}, although there {{GHGheb|text=תָּעֻ֫פָה}} might also, with Qimḥi, be regarded as 2nd masc. For the doubly irregular form {{GHGheb|text=תָּב֫וֹאתָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=33|verse=16}} (explained by Olshausen and König as a scribal error, due to a confusion with {{GHGheb|text=תבואת}} in verse 14), read {{GHGheb|text=תָּב֫וֹאנָה}}. For {{GHGheb|text=תְּבוֹאָֽתְךָ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=22|verse=21}} the noun {{GHGheb|text=תְּבוּאָֽתְךָ|translate=thine increase}}, might be meant, but the Masora has evidently intended an imperfect with the ending ''ath'', instead of {{GHGheb|text=־ָה}}, before the suffix, on the analogy of the 3rd sing. fem. perfect, see {{GHGpar|59|a}}; on {{GHGheb|text=ותבאתי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=25|verse=34}}, see {{GHGpar|76|h}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|48|e}}
The ''cohortative'' expresses the direction of the will to an action and thus denotes especially self-encouragement (in the 1st plur. an exhortation to others at the same time), a resolution or a wish, as an ''optative'', &c., see § 108.

{{GHGmargin-letter|48|f}}
'''4.''' The general characteristic of the {{GHGterm|jussive}} form of the imperfect is rapidity of pronunciation, combined with a tendency to retract<section end=par48 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>
